title: BlueHarbor Health - Redwood Onboarding Kickoff
next_steps: Sofia to share onboarding packet, SOC2 and network diagrams by 2027-11-10
Daniel to schedule a private deployment architecture deep dive for BlueHarbor (wk of 2027-11-15)
Customer to provide sample traffic profile and privacy requirements by 2027-11-12
Priya to create project plan in Confluence and invite stakeholders by 2027-11-11
action_items: Daniel Kim: Draft VPC/network diagram for private deployment (due 2027-11-16)
Sofia Patel: Send pricing sheet and Dedicated capacity options (due 2027-11-10)
Erin Walker: Share token-volume estimates and 99th percentile latency targets (due 2027-11-12)
Jordan Lee: Provide current infra inventory and SSO details (due 2027-11-12)
summary: Kickoff for BlueHarbor Health onboarding. Intro from AE/CSM/SE, high-level overview of Redwood offerings (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private), customer constraints (PHI, VPC requirement, SOC2 compliance), discussion on Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs, next steps and owners assigned.
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Sofia from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, with Daniel our SE and Priya, your CSM. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Erin Walker: Doing well, thanks. Excited to get started.
[00:14] Carlos Mendez: Hey, Carlos here. Quick note — we'll need to keep PHI in mind, so anything we talk about assume that constraint.
[00:22] Sofia Patel: Absolutely, that's front of mind. Today we'll run through the onboarding plan, options for deployment — hosted, dedicated, private — and identify immediate next steps.
[00:30] Daniel Kim: I'll take the tech overview, and we'll dig into the private deployment architecture since I know that's a priority for BlueHarbor.
[00:36] [00:36] Aisha Noor: Great, also curious about inference costs and latency, and how caching/batching would work for our mix of interactive and bulk requests.
[00:45] Priya Singh: We'll surface recommended batching configs and quantization where applicable, and tie that to cost estimates.
[00:52] [01:00] Daniel Kim: Ok quick product overview — Redwood has three primary modes: hosted API for fast time-to-value, Dedicated for reserved GPU capacity, and Private for VPC or on-prem. For customers with PHI and strict network reqs you typically look at Dedicated with VPC peering or the Private deployment, depending on control needs.
[01:20] Carlos Mendez: Can you clarify the difference between Dedicated and Private in terms of tenancy and control?
[01:26] Daniel Kim: Sure. Dedicated is reserved capacity in Redwood's infra, you get isolated GPU pools and an SLA. Network-wise we do vpc peering and egress controls. Private is a customer-controlled control plane in your VPC or on-prem; you manage the network and we provide the software package. So more control, but more ops ownership.
[01:46] Erin Walker: For compliance we probably want Private but we're evaluating the ops overhead. What are the typical lift and timeline?
[01:52] Priya Singh: From other customers' experience, Private deploys can be 4–8 weeks depending on infra readiness and access. Dedicated can be onboarded faster, typically 2–3 weeks for a basic setup and then fine-tuning.
[02:10] [02:10] Jordan Lee: For Private, what's required on our side — s3 buckets, key management, KMS integration?
[02:16] Daniel Kim: Yes you'll provide VPC, subnets, NATing rules, and we integrate with your KMS/HSM for key wrapping. We also support customer-managed S3 or equivalent object stores for model artifacts.
[02:26] Aisha Noor: Are there any differences in model support across modes? Like do we lose certain quantized kernels on Private?
[02:33] Daniel Kim: No, generally parity. There can be additional kernel tuning for specific hardware; if you're using on-prem GPUs like A100s or H100s we validate kernels. We may recommend different quantization profiles for throughput/cost tradeoffs.
[02:50] [03:00] Sofia Patel: Quick qualification — Erin, can you confirm who the champion and exec sponsor are, and target go-live?
[03:06] Erin Walker: I'm the champion, Carlos is the exec sponsor. Target is mid-January for an internal pilot, production by end of Q1.
[03:14] Sofia Patel: Great. And what success metrics are you tracking?
[03:18] Aisha Noor: For the pilot: latency under 300ms 95th, accuracy on our extraction tasks within 2% of baseline, and cost per 1k tokens under a certain threshold — we'll share numbers.
[03:29] [03:30] Daniel Kim: Noted. For latency SLOs we can recommend model variants + batching configs. For interactive low-latency you may want single-request routing to low-latency nodes; for bulk jobs prefer batch pipelines.
[03:42] Carlos Mendez: Any concerns about data residency? We have some EU customers' data that needs to stay in eu-west. Can Redwood route by region?
[03:51] Priya Singh: Yes, we can pin routes by region and set policies to only serve from eu-west. For Private that would be your cluster placement.
[04:00] [04:12] Jordan Lee: On SSO — we use Okta. How does user access and RBAC work in the console?
[04:18] Priya Singh: We integrate with SAML/Okta for SSO, and have RBAC with granular roles — admin, dev, read-only. We'll send the SAML metadata and setup steps.
[04:28] Sofia Patel: I'll include the onboarding checklist with those steps.
[04:32] [04:45] Erin Walker: Security docs — can you share SOC2 reports and your pen-test summary?
[04:49] Sofia Patel: Yes, we'll share SOC 2 Type II and a redacted pen test summary via the secure link.
[04:55] [05:00] Daniel Kim: There's also a technical deep-dive we recommend: we can run a 1-hour benchmarking session where we replay a sample workload to measure latency and cost.
[05:08] Aisha Noor: That would be ideal — we'd like to see 95th pct latency for our top prompt set.
[05:12] Daniel Kim: Perfect. Action item: send instructions for generating sample traffic and the payload schema.
[05:18] [05:30] Sofia Patel: Let's talk about onboarding phases — Phase 1: discovery and infra prep; Phase 2: pilot with sample traffic; Phase 3: fine-tuning and scale; Phase 4: production roll out and SLA handover.
[05:46] Carlos Mendez: Sounds good. Curious about monitoring — what's in the console for traces and token-level cost?
[05:52] Priya Singh: Console gives per-route token cost, latency breakdown, error rates, and traces. We also support exporting metrics to Datadog and setting up alerts.
[06:02] [06:10] Jordan Lee: Do you have an audit log for who invoked which model and data access logs? That's a requirement for us.
[06:16] Daniel Kim: Yes, we provide audit logs and request-level metadata; for Private you can retain logs within your environment.
[06:24] [06:30] Erin Walker: A few practical questions: our infra team prefers Terraform. Do you have IaC modules?
[06:36] Daniel Kim: We provide Terraform modules for VPC peering, IAM roles, and deployment manifests. We'll share the repo link.
[06:42] [06:50] Aisha Noor: On the cost side, if we start hosted for rapid testing then move to Dedicated, is there a big migration effort?
[06:56] Daniel Kim: Migration is straightforward at the API layer — same endpoints and SDKs. Moving models and cache state might need short-lived re-warming, but we have migration guides.
[07:08] Sofia Patel: I'll add migration playbook to the packet.
[07:12] [07:20] Carlos Mendez: Any rate limits or quotas we should plan for during the pilot?
[07:24] Priya Singh: We'll provision burst capacity for pilot traffic and set route-level quotas. We'll also share recommended rate limits based on model choice.
[07:34] [07:45] Jordan Lee: Network egress — do you require static egress IPs for the VPC peering?
[07:50] Daniel Kim: For Dedicated we can provide a set of egress IPs; for Private you control egress.
[07:56] [08:00] Erin Walker: Ok great. Let's talk timelines and resources — who from Redwood will be the day-to-day contact?
[08:06] Priya Singh: I'll be your CSM and main project manager. For technical blockers Daniel will own SE tasks and Sofia is the escalation for commercial items.
[08:16] [08:25] Sofia Patel: Next steps recap — I'll send onboarding packet and pricing; Priya will create the project plan; Daniel will schedule architecture deep dive. Anything to add?
[08:32] Erin Walker: Please include a sample SLA for Dedicated and Private.
[08:36] Sofia Patel: Will do.
[08:40] [09:00] Aisha Noor: Quick question about model versions — does Redwood host our fine-tuned models or do we host them?
[09:06] Daniel Kim: You can either push models to Redwood's model registry or store artifacts in your object store for Private. For Dedicated we typically host models in our registry under restricted access.
[09:18] [09:30] Jordan Lee: For PHI handling, what's the data retention policy? Can we disable request logging?
[09:36] Priya Singh: We support configurable retention windows and the ability to redact or disable logging for certain routes, particularly in Private. We'll provide the data retention config docs.
[09:48] [10:00] Carlos Mendez: Are there any compliance packages or additional controls for healthcare verticals?
[10:06] Sofia Patel: Yes, we offer HIPAA add-ons and can provide BAAs; we'll coordinate legal.
[10:12] [10:20] Erin Walker: Great. Any blockers from our side today?
[10:23] Jordan Lee: We'll need to finalize network contacts and provide Okta metadata — I can get that to you by Friday.
[10:30] Sofia Patel: Thanks Jordan.
[10:32] [10:40] Daniel Kim: For the architecture deep-dive, propose Wed 2027-11-17 at 10am PT?
[10:46] Erin Walker: Works for us.
[10:48] [11:00] Priya Singh: I'll send the invite and include a pre-read with sample prompts and the evaluation criteria.
[11:08] Aisha Noor: One last technical nuance — we have a long-tail of prompts with 1–2k token lengths. How does Redwood handle KV cache and longer contexts?
[11:18] Daniel Kim: We manage KV cache across requests and will recommend kernel profiles and model variants optimized for long context. We also have prefix caching to speed up repeated prefixes.
[11:28] [11:40] Carlos Mendez: Sounds good. Any mention of debugging and tracing for failed requests?
[11:44] Daniel Kim: Console contains request traces and error payloads; for Private you can ship traces to your own tracing backend.
[11:52] [12:00] Sofia Patel: Ok quick recap and owners: Sofia sends onboarding packet and pricing (due 11/10), Daniel drafts VPC diagram and schedules deep-dive (deep-dive 11/17), Priya creates project plan and invite, BlueHarbor provides traffic profile and Okta metadata (due 11/12).
[12:20] Erin Walker: That's perfect, thanks. Excited to get going.
[12:24] Sofia Patel: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up via email with notes and links.
[12:30] [12:30] Call ended.
